title: Clicking a /rankings row opens a popup whose BUY/SELL verdict contradicts the Edge column on the row you just clicked — 83 rows, including 7 of the top 15
claimUnderTest: display-helpers.js's header comment calls the Edge column the single 'market edge' state and says it is 'Always rendered with an explicit state'; trade-logic.js::getPlayerEdge says it 'Reads the backend-stamped marketGapDirection / marketGapMagnitude directly — no client-side recompute'. Both describe the SAME retail-vs-consensus quantity, so a row and its popup should agree.
observed: They use different minimum-gap thresholds on the same quantity: marketAction requires MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF=10 ordinal ranks, getPlayerEdge requires MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP=3. Every row whose gap falls in [3,10) therefore shows HOLD in the table and a full Buy Low / Sell High card in the popup opened from that row. 83 of 1,072 rows are in that band, including Brock Bowers (#2), Bijan Robinson (#3), Drake Maye (#5), Jahmyr Gibbs (#6), Trey McBride (#8), Lamar Jackson (#11), Joe Burrow (#13). Verified in a real browser: the Brock Bowers row renders 'HOLD' + 'Consensus asset', and the popup it opens renders 'Sell High — KTC ranks 5 spots higher than consensus — market overvalues'.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_popup.py   # Playwright, /api/* re-routed to :8000; clicks the Brock Bowers / Trey McBride / Justin Herbert rows on /rankings
reproduction.expected: the Edge column verb and the popup verdict agree for every row
reproduction.actual: Brock Bowers row='HOLD' popup='Sell High'; Trey McBride row='HOLD' popup='Sell High'; Justin Herbert row='HOLD' popup='Buy Low'

numericProof.formula: contradiction iff 3 <= marketGapMagnitude < 10  (or the two verbs are opposite)

userImpact: A user scanning /rankings sees HOLD on his best assets, clicks one to read the detail, and is told to Sell High. Whichever he believes, the other surface told him the opposite about the same player in the same session. There is no indication that two thresholds exist.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F02 claimed 'four different thresholds turn the same backend signal into three contradictory BUY/SELL verdicts on screen simultaneously'. Confirmed and made specific: the thresholds are 0 (backend stamp), 3 (getPlayerEdge), 10 (marketAction) and sourceRankSpread>=20 + rank<=250 (/edge panels), and I have a browser capture of the row/popup disagreement rather than a code reading. Also related to PRIOR-A01-F05.

whatWorks: Both functions read the same effectiveSourceRanks / marketGapMagnitude, so the DIRECTION never disagrees — only the minimum magnitude does. That makes the repair small.
rootCause: Two independently-written thresholds for one quantity, in two files, with no shared constant. thresholds.js exists precisely to be the single source of truth for numeric cutoffs and MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP is not in it — it is a private const inside trade-logic.js.
requiredRepair: Move MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP into frontend/lib/thresholds.js and make getPlayerEdge and marketAction read one constant; add a test that asserts marketAction(row).label and getPlayerEdge(row).signal never disagree on a real contract.

title: The /rankings Edge column labels 32 of 35 top-250 tight ends SELL and every single SELL in the top 250 is a tight end — the 'retail vs expert' gap is measuring TE-premium basis, not mispricing
claimUnderTest: _compute_market_gap's docstring: 'A retail premium means retail ranks the player higher ... i.e. the retail market is pricing the player above where the experts have them.' The /edge page prints 'KTC values these much higher than the expert consensus'. Both frame the gap as a per-player opinion difference.
observed: ktcSfTep is the ONLY source flagged is_retail, and it is a SF-TE++ board. Of the 13 sources on the 'expert consensus' side, the median rank they assign a TE is 9 to 38 places WORSE than KTC's (idpTradeCalc: 115 worse), while for WR/RB/QB the same sources sit 6 to 47 places BETTER than KTC. The gap is therefore a positional level offset between boards. Result on the live board: 65 of 73 TEs with a verb are SELL and only 4 are BUY; inside the top 250 the split is 32 SELL / 3 HOLD / 0 BUY, and all 32 top-250 SELL labels in the entire board are tight ends. The /edge 'Sell signals' panel is 9 of 10 TEs. CLAUDE.md documents (ADR-015) that base-vs-TE++ is a measured 1.209-2.05 multiplier and applies a conversion to VALUES; no equivalent correction is applied to the RANKS this label is computed from, and no caveat appears anywhere on /rankings or /edge.

reproduction.command: node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_te.mjs   # runs the real frontend buildRows + marketAction against curl -b cookies http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data
reproduction.expected: SELL labels distributed across positions roughly in proportion to each position's share of the board (TEs are 73 of 911 analysed rows, ~8%)
reproduction.actual: TE verb distribution {SELL:65, BUY:4, HOLD:4, dash:12}; top-250 SELL labels: 32 of 32 are TE
reproduction.artifact: docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W12/label-matrix.csv + page-probe.json (rendered DOM: 29 SELL in the first 200 rows)

numericProof.formula: P(SELL | TE, rank<=250) vs P(SELL | not TE, rank<=250)

userImpact: A user reading /rankings is told to sell essentially every tight end he owns — Travis Kelce, Mark Andrews, T.J. Hockenson, George Kittle, Kyle Pitts, Dallas Goedert all carry SELL — and to sell them into a league whose scoring is TE-premium, which is exactly the format where TEs are worth the most. The label is a position, wearing a player's name.

priorFinding.note: Prior said '36 of 36 eligible tight ends are labelled SELL, and zero are labelled BUY' on /edge. Reproduced on today's contract with a slightly different population (32/35 in top-250; 65/73 board-wide with 4 BUY) and extended: the same defect drives the /rankings Edge column, which the prior finding did not cover, and I have the per-source median rank deltas that show it is a basis+pool artifact rather than an opinion.

whatWorks: _compute_market_gap correctly EXCLUDES the retail source from the consensus mean, so there is no trivial self-comparison; and marketGapDirection/Magnitude are stamped honestly as 'none'/null when either side is empty.
rootCause: The retail side is a single TE-premium board and the consensus side is mostly non-TE-premium boards drawn from pools of different depth (measured: ktcSfTep 473 rows, idpTradeCalc 901, dlfSf 278, fantasyProsFitzmaurice 298). Raw ordinal ranks from those boards are not commensurable, and no within-position or within-pool normalisation is applied — even though sourceRankMeta[*].percentile is already computed on every row for exactly this purpose.
requiredRepair: Compute the gap as a per-position residual: subtract each source's median rank offset for that position (or compare in percentile space using the already-stamped sourceRankMeta[*].percentile) before differencing retail against consensus. Until then, suppress the verb for TEs or label it 'format basis, not opinion'.
dependencies: Shares a root cause with W12-F008 (idpTradeCalc / fantasyNavigatorSf on the expert side).

title: There is no central Buy/Sell Tracker: 16 label emitters, 14 reachable, 5 competing threshold sets on one quantity, and the two modules built to unify them are one flag-off and one caller-less
claimUnderTest: The product requirement is a central Buy/Sell Tracker that is the broad primary recommendation system and is NOT the same feature as Consensus Edge. src/consensus_edge/__init__.py already states the problem in the repo's own words: 'The platform accumulated six overlapping answers to "is this player a buy?" ... "Buy" means a different thing on each screen. This package is the single answer.'
observed: No module, route, page, table or state key is a central tracker. I enumerated 16 independent directional emitters (docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W12/label-families.json); 14 are reachable today. FIVE of them apply different cutoffs to the SAME retail-vs-consensus quantity: >0 (backend stamp), >=3 (getPlayerEdge, powers PlayerPopup and the /league Edge Map), >=10 (marketAction, powers the /rankings Edge column), sourceRankSpread>=20 AND rank<=250 (/edge panels and the /rankings rail), and >=10 on a different source set (idpMarketAction, /edge IDP tab). None of the 14 shares state, imports another, or reads another's output. The two candidates for an arbiter both fail: src/consensus_edge/* returns 503 on every route because the flag defaults off, and src/news/unified_signal_engine.py — 352 lines whose docstring calls it 'Unified signal engine — single entry point for every BUY/SELL/HOLD decision emitted to users' — is imported by nothing outside tests and one audit script.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'unified_signal_engine' --include=*.py . | grep -v __pycache__ | grep -v '^./tests'   # 3 hits, all comments/docstrings, zero imports;  then: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/consensus-edge/top
reproduction.expected: one module that produces the platform's directional recommendation, consumed by every surface
reproduction.actual: unified_signal_engine has no production importer; /api/consensus-edge/top -> 503 {"error":"feature_disabled","flag":"consensus_edge"}; 14 other emitters serve users

numericProof.formula: count of distinct modules that emit a BUY/SELL/HOLD-class verb to a user surface

userImpact: Every screen answers 'should I buy this player' with a different rule and none of them says which one is authoritative or that the others exist. A user cannot form a consistent policy, and cannot tell whether two screens disagreeing means new information or just two constants.

priorFinding.note: Prior said 'Four independent BUY/SELL label families run on the same players with four different threshold sets and no reconciliation'. Confirmed and expanded: the count is 16 emitters / 14 reachable, and the four-way threshold split is specifically FIVE cutoffs on one quantity. Prior did not record that consensus_edge was designed as the arbiter or that unified_signal_engine has no caller.

whatWorks: src/consensus_edge is the correct shape for the missing arbiter: it consumes other engines as components, renormalises weights over PRESENT components, refuses to score without a core component, forces Conflicted when strong evidence opposes, and separates direction from confidence. It is switched off for an honest reason (its top-20 buy list did not beat a random draw) rather than hidden.
rootCause: Every new surface added its own label rather than consuming an existing one, and no module was ever made authoritative. The two attempts to consolidate were both left unreachable.
requiredRepair: Pick one emitter as the tracker. The cheapest honest version: promote the retail-vs-consensus family to a single backend-stamped verb (one threshold, computed once in _compute_market_gap) that every surface renders verbatim, and demote the other emitters to explicitly-labelled secondary lenses. Then decide whether consensus_edge or unified_signal_engine is the long-term arbiter and delete the other.
dependencies: W12-F001, W12-F002, W12-F004, W12-F008 are all instances of this.

title: /edge's Buy and Sell panels rank and headline sourceRankSpread — total dispersion across all 13 sources — under prose that says it is the KTC-vs-consensus gap; the headline number overstates the real gap by a median 5.6x and up to 30x
claimUnderTest: The /edge panel subtitle reads 'KTC values these much higher than the expert consensus' and the column is headed SPREAD. edge-helpers' topRetailPremium returns detail: `Sell +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks`, presenting the spread as the size of the buy/sell edge.
observed: Direction comes from marketGapDirection (retail mean vs consensus mean) but the GATE and the SORT and the printed number are all sourceRankSpread = max(effectiveSourceRanks) - min(effectiveSourceRanks), a completely different quantity. The row the live page ranks #2 in 'Sell signals', De'Zhaun Stribling, is displayed at +/-181 while his actual retail-vs-consensus gap (marketGapMagnitude) is 5.9 ranks — below the 10-rank floor the /rankings Edge column uses, which is why that same player renders HOLD there. Across the 20 rows the two panels actually show, spread/gap ratios run 2.7x to 30.5x, median 5.6x.

reproduction.expected: the number the panel prints equals the retail-vs-consensus gap it describes (marketGapMagnitude)
reproduction.actual: Eli Raridon printed 332, real gap 44.3 (7.5x); De'Zhaun Stribling printed 181, real gap 5.9 (30.5x); Jacoby Brissett printed 152, real gap 11.8 (12.8x)

numericProof.formula: sourceRankSpread / marketGapMagnitude, which should be 1.0 if the printed number were the described gap

userImpact: The ordering of the trade board is wrong: players are ranked as the biggest sells by total source noise, not by how far the market is from the experts. A user works the list top-down and starts with the noisiest row, not the most mispriced one.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with live numbers. I also tested PRIOR-A05-F02 ('38% of rows in /edge's Buy/Sell panels render as HOLD in the /rankings Edge column') and could NOT reproduce that magnitude: on today's contract it is 1 of 20 rows (5%) — De'Zhaun Stribling. Relation for PRIOR-A05-F02 is 'partial': the phenomenon is real and has the same root cause as this finding, but the rate I measure is 5%, not 38%.

whatWorks: marketGapMagnitude is stamped on every row and is the correct quantity; the panels only have to read it instead of sourceRankSpread.
rootCause: The gate was written before marketGapMagnitude existed and was never migrated; sourceRankSpread was the only per-row dispersion number available at the time.
requiredRepair: Gate and sort the /edge panels and the /rankings rail on marketGapMagnitude, print that number, and keep sourceRankSpread as a separate 'source disagreement' column if it is still wanted.
dependencies: Fixing this also resolves the /edge-vs-/rankings mismatch counted in PRIOR-A05-F02.

title: The 12-hour signal-alert cooldown is keyed on the rule TAG, so it never engages when the reason changes — which is exactly what changes when a signal flips — and the email then renders the flip as a first-ever signal
claimUnderTest: signal_alerts.py: '_MIN_NOTIFY_INTERVAL_HOURS: Minimum hours between alerts for the same (user, signalKey). Stops a rapid-fire RISK -> SELL -> RISK flicker from spamming.'
observed: state_key is aliasSignalKey or signalKey, and BOTH embed the rule tag (`sid:<sleeperId>::<tag>` / `<name>::<tag>`, built by terminal.py::_signal_key / _signal_alias_key). A different firing rule is therefore a different state row with prev_signal='' and prev_notified_at=0, so the cooldown branch is skipped entirely and the alert fires immediately. Executed against a scratch user_kv: RISK/alert_with_drop then RISK/high_vol_drop fired twice with zero elapsed time, and BUY/uptrend_controlled then SELL/sustained_downtrend fired twice with zero elapsed time. Because prev_signal is empty on the new key, priorSignal is None and format_alert_email prints '— -> SELL', so the digest presents a reversal as a brand-new signal. The digest also counts one player twice ('2 of your players had a signal change').

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_cooldown.py  (source reproduced verbatim in the artifact header; writes only to a scratchpad sqlite)
reproduction.expected: the second alert for the same player inside 12 hours is suppressed, or at minimum carries priorSignal='BUY'
reproduction.actual: fired=1 for both calls; stored keys are sid:4984::uptrend_controlled and sid:4984::sustained_downtrend; both transitions carry priorSignal=None

numericProof.formula: suppressed iff prev_notified_at and now - prev_notified_at < 12*3600*1000, evaluated on state[alias_key] where alias_key contains the tag

userImpact: A user is emailed 'Josh Allen — -> SELL' hours after being emailed 'Josh Allen — -> BUY', with nothing in either message saying the other happened. The guard that was written to prevent exactly this is bypassed by the thing it was meant to catch.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index. PRIOR-A23-F09 is a different alert defect (marked delivered before delivery is attempted); PRIOR-A05-F13 / PRIOR-A22-F05 / PRIOR-A23-F06 are about custom_alerts value_crosses being a level test.

whatWorks: bdvm_signal_alerts.py keys its state on `bdvm:<playerId>` with no tag, so its 12h guard does work; and its baseline-seeding pass genuinely prevents a flag-on flood. That module is the correct pattern.
rootCause: The tag is in the key for a legitimate reason — dismissals are meant to follow the reason, so a new reason re-surfaces a dismissed player — but the same key was reused for the notification cooldown, where the tag must NOT participate.
requiredRepair: Split the two keys: keep `<name|sid>::<tag>` for dismissal lifecycle, and cool down on `sid:<sleeperId>` alone. Carry prev_signal across tags so priorSignal is truthful, and de-duplicate players in format_alert_email's count.

title: Three independent email-sending detectors can alert on the same player on the same day, to the same address, with three separate cooldown namespaces and no cross-check
claimUnderTest: bdvm_signal_alerts.py states it is 'Deliberately a SEPARATE detector from signal_alerts.py' with a different state namespace 'so terminal keys can never collide'. The stated benefit is isolation.
observed: Isolation of STATE is achieved; isolation of the USER is not. All three read the same user_kv field notificationsEmail and all three call _deliver_email_smtp. signal_alerts and bdvm_signal_alerts run inside the SAME sweep, back to back, over the same roster (server.py:11695 then :11712), so one player in one sweep can produce two emails. custom_alerts runs from its own route over the same playersArray and can add a third. Their vocabularies are disjoint and opposite-capable: {RISK, SELL, BUY, MONITOR} from rank-history movement versus {STRONG_BUY, BUY, SELL, STRONG_SELL} from fundamental-minus-market alpha. Nothing compares them, and no message mentions the other detector.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'process_user_alerts\|process_user_bdvm_alerts' server.py   # 11695 and 11712, same loop iteration, same `email` local;  grep -n 'notificationsEmail' server.py   # 10278 (custom) and 11609 (signal+bdvm)
reproduction.expected: one per-player decision reaches the user's inbox
reproduction.actual: three detectors, one address, three cooldown namespaces (signalAlertStateByLeague / bdvmSignalAlertStateByLeague / customAlertsState), zero cross-references

numericProof.formula: count of modules calling _deliver_email_smtp with a per-player directional verb

userImpact: Two emails about the same player can arrive minutes apart telling him to buy and to sell, each looking authoritative and neither acknowledging the other. Because the label sets differ, he cannot even tell they are about the same question.
whatWorks: bdvm_signal_alerts' baseline-seeding (first sweep per user+league records silently) is a genuinely good mechanism and is test-pinned; and both detectors degrade to an error field in the sweep summary rather than failing the sweep.
rootCause: Each detector was added as an independent feature with its own state, and the delivery step was never centralised.
requiredRepair: Introduce one per-(user, league, sweep) digest that collects candidate alerts from all detectors, resolves same-player conflicts explicitly (show both with their reasons, or suppress on disagreement), and sends once.
dependencies: W12-F003. Any central tracker would own this.

title: Direction is never gated on confidence: 253 of the 356 directional verbs on /rankings sit on rows the same page badges as low or no confidence, and 102 rest on a 'consensus' of two sources or fewer
claimUnderTest: edge-helpers.js header: 'Nothing is predicted or editorialized. Every label traces to a measurable property of the source data.' The /edge page states 'Every signal here is derived from measurable properties of the data — how many sources cover a player, how closely they agree'.
observed: marketAction, idpMarketAction and getPlayerEdge read no confidence field at all — not confidenceBucket, not sourceCount, not isSingleSource, not anomalyFlags. On the live contract 356 rows carry BUY or SELL from marketAction; 173 of them are confidenceBucket 'low', 80 are 'none', and 5 carry anomaly flags. 102 of the 356 have at most two sources on the entire consensus side. Every future draft pick gets SELL from a two-row comparison (ktcSfTep vs idpTradeCalc) — two crowd trade calculators framed as 'retail versus expert consensus'. The rule engines are worse in a different way: signal-engine.js and terminal._evaluate_signal emit no confidence field whatsoever, and the one rule that read confidence was retired in 2026-07-30 because the metric is structurally capped at 0.59375.

reproduction.expected: a directional verb requires enough evidence to support it, or is downgraded / suppressed

numericProof.formula: share of BUY/SELL labels on rows the same UI badges low/none confidence = 253/356

userImpact: A bold SELL sits in the same column, in the same style, whether it rests on 13 agreeing sources or on two crowd calculators. The confidence badge is two columns to the left and does not modify the verb, so a user has no reason to read them together.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A12-F03/F04 are about confidenceBucket itself being wrong (raisable by missing data; measuring percentile agreement rather than value agreement). This is the adjacent, independent defect: whatever confidenceBucket means, no directional label consults it.

whatWorks: src/consensus_edge/score.py::classify is the counter-example and gets it right: direction and confidence are computed separately, INSUFFICIENT is returned below a confidence floor, a Strong label is downgraded to a plain one when confidence is short, and CONFLICTED beats the arithmetic. It is switched off.
rootCause: The label functions were written as pure formatters over one field pair and never grew an evidence gate.
requiredRepair: Give marketAction / getPlayerEdge a confidence argument: suppress the verb (render an explicit 'thin evidence' state, not a dash) when confidenceBucket is low/none or the consensus side has fewer than 3 sources.

title: KTC is on both sides of the 'KTC versus expert consensus' comparison, and a crowd trade calculator is the 'expert' on one page and the 'market' on three others
claimUnderTest: _compute_market_gap frames 'the retail market (sources flagged is_retail in the registry — today just KTC) against every other registered source (the expert consensus)'.
observed: Two sources are on the wrong side. (a) fantasyNavigatorSf carries correlation_group 'ktc' and the registry's own comment says it 'republishes KTC-derived numbers, so the two are not independent votes' — yet is_retail is False, so KTC-derived ranks are averaged into the EXPERT mean on 368 rows; removing it changes the /rankings Edge verb on 29 of them, including Nico Collins (#40, BUY -> HOLD) and Breece Hall (#54, BUY -> HOLD). (b) idpTradeCalc has no is_retail flag at all, so it is an 'expert' here — while its own registry entry calls it 'the retail IDP authority', src/bdvm/market.py lists it in VALUE_MARKET_SOURCES tagged 'crowd', src/trade/finder.py uses it as the retail market anchor for IDP, and display-helpers.js::idpMarketAction uses it as the retail anchor on /edge's IDP tab. It sits on the expert side of 419 rows; removing it changes the verb on 103 of them, and of the BUY<->SELL reversals every one is a tight end.

reproduction.command: node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_dbl.mjs  (and w12_flip.mjs for the retail-side reclassification)
reproduction.expected: no source contributes to both sides of the comparison, and one source has one role platform-wide
reproduction.actual: fantasyNavigatorSf on the expert side for 368 rows / 29 verb changes; idpTradeCalc on the expert side for 419 rows / 103 verb changes; moving idpTradeCalc to the retail side flips 101 SELL->BUY

numericProof.formula: recompute marketAction with the source dropped from / moved across the retail set and diff the verb

userImpact: The 'edge' the page reports is partly KTC disagreeing with a republication of itself, and partly one crowd calculator disagreeing with another while being labelled the expert view. A user acting on the gap is not acting on the information he is told he is acting on.

priorFinding.note: Prior said idpTradeCalc's offense ranks sit a median 104 ranks below the rest of the consensus and flip the verdict on 10.6% of offense rows. Confirmed with a per-position breakdown (median +76 QB / +78 WR / +83 RB / +115 TE) and a larger flip count on my denominator (103 of the 419 rows where both KTC and IDPTC rank the player, 24.6%). The fantasyNavigatorSf half is not in the prior index and is new.

whatWorks: The registry already knows the truth — correlation_group 'ktc' exists and is documented, and is_cross_market marks idpTradeCalc as a market source. The facts needed for the fix are already stamped; only _retail_source_keys() ignores them.
rootCause: _retail_source_keys() reads a single boolean that was set per source ad hoc, and never consults correlation_group. idpTradeCalc's is_retail was simply never set, so `s.get('is_retail')` returns None and it defaults to the expert side.
requiredRepair: Derive the retail set from correlation_group plus an explicit market-vs-expert taxonomy field, and give idpTradeCalc one role platform-wide. If it is the retail anchor for IDP it cannot be an expert for offense.
dependencies: Shares a root cause with W12-F002.

title: The terminal home page prescribes opposite actions from the same rank-history input: the Movers panel calls a riser a sell-high candidate while the Signals panel directly below calls the same rise a BUY
claimUnderTest: MoversPanel's in-code comment: 'A riser's price has already gone UP, so it is a candidate to sell HIGH — not to buy low.' signal-engine.js's buy.uptrend_controlled: a 7-day rank rise of +3 or more with non-high volatility is BUY, reason '7d trend of +N and volatility is low'.
observed: Both panels render on the terminal home page, both are driven by data/rank_history.jsonl ordinal deltas, and they prescribe opposite actions for the same movement. Movers is a momentum-REVERSAL thesis at a 15-rank threshold; the signal engine is a momentum-FOLLOWING thesis at a 3-rank threshold. A player who rose 20 ranks in 7 days is simultaneously a 'SELL-HIGH CANDIDATE' in one panel and 'BUY' in the other. Neither thesis has ever been validated against an outcome, neither panel references the other, and no copy anywhere tells the user they are different theories rather than different facts.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_page2.py   # renders / with /api/* re-routed; body contains 'RISERS — SELL-HIGH CANDIDATES' and 'Signals / Rule-driven Buy / Sell / Hold per roster player' on one page
reproduction.expected: one directional interpretation of a rank rise per page
reproduction.actual: MoversPanel: riser -> sell-high. signal-engine buy.uptrend_controlled: trend7 >= +3 -> BUY. Same page, same input, opposite verbs.

numericProof.formula: sign of the prescribed action for delta > 0

userImpact: The two most prominent widgets on the landing page give a user opposite instructions about the same player from the same number, with no way to tell which the product believes.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A05-F12 and PRIOR-A23-F08 both claim 'MoversPanel labels risers as buy-low candidates and fallers as sell-high — both inverted'. That is NOT true at HEAD e96c06ef. The source at MoversPanel.jsx:196-215 reads 'Risers — sell-high candidates' / 'Fallers — buy-low candidates', carries a comment recording the correction as 'audit finding S-8', and the rendered DOM confirms it. Both prior findings are already fixed. What survives is a different and larger problem — the corrected polarity is now the exact opposite of the signal engine on the same page — which is recorded here as new.

whatWorks: The Movers polarity itself is now correct and the fix is documented in-code. /api/movers also degrades honestly: with no history it returns risers:[] fallers:[] plus historyDepthDays:0 rather than inventing movement.
rootCause: Two panels were written from two different trading theses and neither was ever chosen as the product's position.
requiredRepair: Pick one thesis, state it in the UI, and make the other panel descriptive rather than prescriptive ('biggest movers' with no buy/sell framing) until one is validated against realized outcomes.

title: The /rankings Edge column promises it is 'never an ambiguous dash' and renders a dash for all 398 IDP rows; the IDP buy/sell verb exists only on /edge
claimUnderTest: The Edge column's headerInfo tooltip: 'Market edge: retail (KTC) vs expert consensus. Always rendered with an explicit state — never an ambiguous dash.'
observed: KTC publishes no IDP, so every IDP row has an empty retail side and marketEdge returns kind 'consensus_only', which marketAction maps to the label '—'. All 398 IDP rows on the board render the dash the tooltip promises never appears. display-helpers.js contains a complete IDP equivalent (idpMarketEdge / idpMarketAction, IDPTC as the anchor) that /rankings does not call — it is wired only into the /edge IDP tab. On the live board that helper produces a directional verb for a meaningful share of IDP rows: e.g. Carson Schwesinger (LB, board rank 42) is SELL on /edge and a dash on /rankings; Caleb Downs (DB, rank 150) likewise.

reproduction.expected: explicit state on every row, per the tooltip

userImpact: In an IDP league (this one is idpEnabled) 37% of the board carries no market signal on the main board, and a defender the /edge page says to sell shows nothing on /rankings. A user who only reads /rankings concludes there is no edge on defenders.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A05-F17 says the IDP Buy/Sell comparison averages effective ranks that are not on a common scale — a defect in idpMarketAction itself. This is the adjacent gap: /rankings does not call it at all, so the tooltip's own promise is broken on 398 rows.

whatWorks: /edge does route IDP rows through the IDPTC-anchored helper and labels the sections 'IDP sell signals' / 'IDP buy signals', so the anchor swap is disclosed there.
rootCause: The Edge column was written for the offense board and the IDP helper was added later on a different page.
requiredRepair: Have the /rankings Edge column dispatch on assetClass — idpMarketAction for IDP rows, marketAction for offense — and label the anchor in the tooltip. Or correct the tooltip.
dependencies: Fixing this without fixing PRIOR-A05-F17 propagates that defect to a bigger surface.

title: Both live rule engines return HOLD 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers' for 665 of 665 rostered players because the rank-history log does not exist, and no surface says the evidence is missing
claimUnderTest: signal-engine.js: 'HOLD never fires as a rule — it's the fallback when nothing else does', with the user-facing reason 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.'
observed: data/rank_history.jsonl (the path in rank_history.py:74) is absent from this container, so GET /api/data/rank-history returns {"days":30,"history":{}}. Every context therefore has trend7=null, trend30=null and volatility=null, no rule can fire, and every player falls to HOLD. Queried all 12 teams: 665 of 665 rostered players return HOLD with the tag default_hold and that exact reason string. The reason asserts stability as a positive finding when the truth is that nothing was measured — 'we looked and it is quiet' and 'we have no data' render identically. /api/movers does better on the same missing input: it returns historyDepthDays:0 alongside the empty lists.

reproduction.command: for t in $(curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(" ".join(x["ownerId"] for x in json.load(sys.stdin)["availableTeams"]))'); do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal?ownerId=$t"; done | python3 -c 'import sys,json,collections;c=collections.Counter();[c.update(s["signal"] for s in json.loads(l)["signals"]) for l in sys.stdin]; print(c)'
reproduction.expected: a mix of verdicts, or an explicit 'no history' state
reproduction.actual: Counter({'HOLD': 665}) — every rostered player, every team, reason 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.'

userImpact: The Signals panel reports a calm, healthy roster when in fact it has measured nothing. Its default filter shows RISK/SELL/MONITOR/BUY, so the panel renders empty and reads as 'no issues' rather than 'no data'.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly, and quantified across all 12 rosters. Also confirms PRIOR-A18-F21 (rank_history.jsonl absent from the repository) as the cause. Note the protocol's data-absence caveat applies to the emptiness; the finding is the WORDING, which is a code property and would mislead in production during any scrape lapse.

whatWorks: The null-guards themselves are correct and deliberate: sell.sustained_downtrend and strong.elite_stable both test `trend30 != null` rather than coalescing to 0, with an in-code note that a `?? 0` once made unmeasured history satisfy `<= 0` and emit SELL. The engine fails safe. Both engines are also pinned to one shared fixture (tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json).
rootCause: HOLD is overloaded: it is both 'measured, nothing happening' and 'not measured'. The reason string only describes the first.
requiredRepair: Return a distinct verdict (e.g. NO_DATA, tag 'no_history') when trend7, trend30 and volatility are all null, and have BuySellHold / TopSignalsRail render it as an evidence gap rather than folding it into HOLD.
dependencies: data/rank_history.jsonl must exist for the engines to do anything at all.

title: src/news/unified_signal_engine.py declares itself 'the single entry point for every BUY/SELL/HOLD decision emitted to users' and has no production caller
claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'Unified signal engine — single entry point for every BUY/SELL/HOLD decision emitted to users ... Cooldown is ONE cooldown table keyed on (user, league, signalKey) — multi-source signals for the same player don't spam the user multiple times.'
observed: 352 lines defining UnifiedSignal (verdict + confidence 0..1 + severity + source_class + explanation) and a resolver that merges value / usage / injury / transaction signals. Nothing in src/ or server.py imports it. The only references are tests/news/test_unified_signal_engine.py, tests/news/test_usage_signal_calibration.py, scripts/audit/measure_usage_signal_rate.py, and two comments. Its `usage_signals` input flag is documented OFF for two independent reasons (no consumer; the detector fires on 17.8% of active players weekly). The real cooldown table it describes is the one in signal_alerts.py — which, per W12-F005, is keyed on the rule tag and does exactly the spamming this docstring says it prevents.

reproduction.actual: 3 hits: src/api/feature_flags.py:75 and :332 (comments), src/consensus_edge/__init__.py:7 (a docstring calling it 'a never-wired news.unified_signal_engine')

numericProof.formula: count of non-test modules importing the module

userImpact: None directly — it is unreachable. The harm is to maintainers: it is the most authoritative-sounding description of the platform's signal architecture and it describes nothing that runs, which makes the real behaviour harder to find.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index as a finding, although src/api/feature_flags.py and src/consensus_edge/__init__.py both already state it in-repo. Recorded so the census of directional emitters is complete.

whatWorks: feature_flags.py already classifies usage_signals as NO_GATE/OFF with the measured reason, and tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py re-measures reachability against the real import graph on every run. That mechanism is exactly right and caught this.
rootCause: Built ahead of its inputs; the inputs were then measured and rejected, and the module was left in place.
requiredRepair: Either wire it (and delete the emitters it replaces) or delete it and move its useful ideas — one cooldown table, confidence carried beside verdict, severity from roster impact — into whichever module becomes the tracker.

title: Every movement threshold is an absolute ordinal-rank count applied uniformly across a 1,092-row board, so a 3-rank move is a SELL at rank 900 and not a signal at rank 1
claimUnderTest: signal-engine.js: 'No random labels: every signal is produced by a named rule whose boolean test evaluates known inputs.' The rules are stated as universal thresholds (trend7 <= -3, trend7 <= -5, MAD <= 1 / <= 4, value >= 7000).
observed: _window_trend returns baseline_rank - latest_rank, a raw ordinal difference, and _volatility takes the MAD of raw ordinal deltas. Both are compared against fixed integers across a board whose ranks span 1 to 1,092. Moving from rank 5 to rank 8 and from rank 905 to rank 908 both produce trend7 = -3 and both fire sell.sustained_downtrend, which is in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS and therefore emails. Conversely the #1 overall player dropping two spots — a far larger real repricing — fires nothing. The 'high volatility' label needs MAD > 4 ranks, which is near-certain deep on the board and near-impossible at the top, so RISK and MONITOR are structurally concentrated in the tail. /api/movers uses a fourth constant on the same scale (15 ranks). None of the four thresholds is depth-scaled, and the pipeline already stamps a percentile per source per row.

reproduction.command: sed -n '338,371p;897,983p' src/api/terminal.py   # _window_trend / _volatility / _evaluate_signal;  curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/movers | python3 -m json.tool | head -5   # "threshold": 15
reproduction.expected: a movement threshold that scales with board depth, or a percentile/value-based trigger
reproduction.actual: trend7 <= -3, trend7 <= -5, MAD 1 and 4, movers 15 — all raw ordinal ranks, all constant across 1,092 rows

numericProof.formula: a fixed ordinal threshold implies a value threshold that varies with the local slope of the Hill curve; the slope near rank 1 is roughly an order of magnitude steeper than near rank 900

userImpact: The alerting is loudest about the players who matter least. A user who acts on the emails spends attention on tail moves and is never told when a top-10 asset repriced.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A12-F00 makes the same class of argument about marketGapDirection averaging ordinal ranks across pools of different depth — confirmed separately in W12-F002/F008. This is the time-series analogue: the same ordinal-ranks-are-not-commensurable error applied to movement over time rather than across sources. Recorded as partial because the prior finding does not cover the rule engines or /api/movers. Confidence is medium because with rank_history.jsonl absent I could not measure the realized firing distribution by depth, only derive it from the thresholds and the curve.

whatWorks: The thresholds are at least identical on both sides of the Python/JS parity boundary and are pinned by tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json, so a change on one side fails both suites.
rootCause: The rules were written against ordinal ranks because that is what rank_history.jsonl stores, and no depth normalisation was added.
requiredRepair: Express movement in value space (rank_history already stores rankDerivedValue alongside rank) or as a percentile delta, and re-derive the constants against the realized distribution once history exists.
dependencies: Needs data/rank_history.jsonl to re-derive the constants empirically.

title: Two documented constants in the label layer are wrong or dead: edge-helpers states the Edge premium rank cap as 150 while the constant is 250, and MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD is imported and never used
claimUnderTest: edge-helpers.js::isTopRankedForEdgePremium docstring: 'inside the top ``EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT`` (150 today) on the blended board'. thresholds.js: 'Bumped 150 -> 250 (2026-04-29) ... the KTC-only path pulled in low-rated players KTC happened to price highly (Mac Jones, Jacoby Brissett, etc.) which defeated the "only trade-relevant" intent.'
observed: EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT is 250; the docstring beside the function that consumes it says 150. Separately, MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD (30) is imported at edge-helpers.js:17 and referenced nowhere in the module — actionLabel's 'Market premium' branch was removed and the import survived; only the test file still exercises the constant. And the named counterexample is live: Jacoby Brissett is currently row 5 of /edge's 'Buy signals' panel (consensus rank 247, inside the 250 cap), so the fix described in that comment does not achieve its stated intent.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD' frontend/ --include=*.js --include=*.jsx | grep -v node_modules   # thresholds.js:29 (definition), edge-helpers.js:17 (import), and only __tests__ thereafter;  then read docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W12/page-probe.json '/edge'.bodyExcerpt
reproduction.expected: docstrings match the constants; imports are used; the named counterexample is excluded
reproduction.actual: docstring says 150 / constant is 250; MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD unused in src; 'Jacoby Brissett ARI QB ±152 2,418' is row 5 of the live Buy signals panel

userImpact: Minimal for a reader of the page; real for a maintainer changing the cap, who will trust the docstring next to the function over the constant two files away.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A05-F19 (150 vs 250 docstring) and PRIOR-A05-F20 (MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD imported and never used) both confirmed by reading HEAD. The Jacoby Brissett observation — that the comment's own named counterexample is on the live page — is new.

whatWorks: thresholds.js does centralise the cutoffs it owns and carries the change history for them.
rootCause: A constant was changed in one file and its prose description in another was not.
requiredRepair: Delete the number from the docstring (reference the constant by name only), drop the unused import, and either widen the exclusion rule or stop naming Jacoby Brissett as an example of what it excludes.

title: Verified working: the only two label families with a documented, calibrated-or-honestly-uncalibrated score both refuse to show a number rather than fake one — /consensus-edge and /bdvm degrade to specific, truthful empty states
claimUnderTest: The prompt asks whether a summary score in [-100,+100] has a documented meaning and is calibrated, and whether the system ever emits HOLD / NO SIGNAL on thin evidence.
observed: consensus_edge's composite is 100*tanh(sum of renormalised weights times clamped component scores), with bands +-30/+-60 and confidence gates 35/50/70 — all in config/consensus_edge/params_v1.json, each carrying an explicit _status ('prior') and a _rationale saying the bands are NOT calibrated ('with a single validated component there is no basis for asserting that +60 means anything different in kind from +55'). COMPONENT_VALIDATION records mispricing as measured-null (rho +0.031 over 6 folds, beaten by a plain buy-cheap benchmark in 5 of 6), sharpFlow as unmeasurABLE, opportunity as measured-and-rejected at weight 0.0 — and score.py::composite excludes zero-weight components from componentsPresent so a rejected signal cannot inflate confidence. classify() is the only function in the platform that separates direction from confidence, returns INSUFFICIENT below a floor, downgrades Strong to plain when confidence is short, and forces CONFLICTED rather than averaging opposing evidence to Neutral. The whole package is behind a flag that defaults off with the reason stated in the 503 body and on the page. /bdvm likewise renders 'No projection snapshot yet ... this season's hasn't been built yet' rather than a board.

reproduction.expected: an honest disabled/no-data state, not a fabricated board
reproduction.actual: 503 {"error":"feature_disabled","flag":"consensus_edge","message":"...did not beat a random draw from the same priced universe in any measured fold..."}; page renders 'Consensus Edge is switched off' with the same reason; /bdvm renders 'No projection snapshot yet'

numericProof.formula: score = 100 * tanh( sum_i (w_i / sum w) * clamp(v_i, -1, 1) ) over PRESENT components only

userImpact: None — this is the behaviour the rest of the label layer should copy.

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified positive per the protocol's instruction that proving something works is as valuable as finding a defect.

whatWorks: Direction and confidence computed separately; absent components dropped and weights renormalised rather than treated as zero; zero-weight components reported in their own bucket so they can neither hide as missing data nor inflate coverage; conflict forces a refusal instead of averaging to Neutral; every parameter carries _status and _weightProvenance; the flag default is justified by a measured null rather than a preference.
requiredRepair: None. Use src/consensus_edge/score.py as the template when consolidating the other 13 emitters (W12-F003).
